name: Adaiah
overview: Adaiah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known specifically as the son of Jeroham. His mention in Scripture is concise, with no additional personal details or notable events recorded beyond his lineage. As a Levite, Adaiah belonged to the priestly tribe set apart for service to God.
namesAndTitles: The name Adaiah means 'adornment of YHWH,' reflecting a connection to the Lord's honor and beauty. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:12 and was not specifically given by God but carries a theologically significant meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Adaiah explicitly as the son of Jeroham. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Adaiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Levi, emphasizing the continuity of Levitical families dedicated to God's service. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:12 situates him within the post-exilic community, underscoring the restoration of the priestly order and the faithfulness of God's covenant people. Although not a prominent figure in narrative events, Adaiah represents the faithful lineage through which God preserved His worship and law.
